subject: Standby activation ownership, timeline and costing clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@stratuspay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 14:12:00 +0000
Subject: Standby activation ownership & timeline - clarifying scope

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — StratusPay is close to a decision but procurement has flagged a few items we need clarified before we move forward on the Dedicated contract. Specifically:

- During a regional outage, what exactly does Redwood expect the customer to own vs Redwood for the standby activation (DNS cutover, traffic routing, runbook execution)?
- Can you confirm typical RTO/RPO numbers we should plan for under the Dedicated SLA vs a Warm-Standby addendum?
- Is there a lead time (hours/days) required to bring KV caches/replicas fully online before traffic switchover?
- How is pricing handled while the standby is active vs after full failover? And do you bill for the warm standby window if we never fail over?

Procurement would like a short addendum we can review with their legal team that specifies responsibilities and any temporary credits during an activation window. Can you point me to an example or draft wording?

If easier, happy to do a 30-min call — Ingrid (ops@stratuspay.com) is copied and will own the technical checklist.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Wu
Head of Platform Reliability
StratusPay

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@stratuspay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Standby activation ownership & timeline - clarifying scope

Hi Alex — great questions. I pulled together the short answers below and a suggested next step. Attaching a provisional pricing sheet for warm-standby sizing (provisional-standby-pricing-v1.pdf).

Short answers:
- Ownership: Redwood will manage the failover playbook execution inside our control plane (activation of reserved pools, model routing, and if enabled, automated DNS failover hooks). The customer remains responsible for application-level routing adjustments, signed DNS delegation (if you keep DNS), and any on-prem networking steps. We can operate DNS failover on your behalf under a managed-delegation addendum; that requires documented access and an emergency contact.

- RTO / RPO: Our standard Dedicated tiers include:
  * Reserved (hot): RTO <= 1 minute, RPO <= 0 (replicated synchronously)
  * Warm-standby (preferred for cost): RTO 15–30 minutes, RPO up to 5 minutes (async replication + KV cache rebuild)
  * Cold/warm blended: RTO 1–4 hours, RPO up to 1 hour (lower cost)

- KV cache warmup: Typical KV cache convergence depends on sequence distribution; for a warm-standby config we recommend a 15–40 minute warmup window to reach >90% hit rates for common prefixes. We provide cache pre-warming scripts and a designated warm-up API endpoint to accelerate this.

- Pricing during standby vs after failover: We bill reserved capacity for the standby pool while it is allocated. If customer traffic shifts to the standby (i.e., declared failover), standard Dedicated billing applies post-failover. For customers who require a billing cap during an activation window we can offer a temporary credit structure in the addendum (we've seen typical pilot credits of 25–50% for the first 72 hours while the failover window is validated).

Next steps:
1) Kimberly / Neha will prepare a concise addendum with: exact RTO/RPO numbers, ownership bullets (DNS/delegation, runbook responsibilities), and a proposed temporary credit clause.
2) We can run a 30-day pilot where we set up a warm-standby in the secondary region and exercise a controlled switchover to validate the 15–30 minute RTO.
3) If you agree, we’ll lock in a pilot start date and share a short checklist for the network/DNS items.

Would Thursday next week work for a 30-min alignment call?

—Sean

Sean — thanks for the fast follow-up. A couple of technical clarifications from our side (I’m copying the relevant excerpt from your message inline):

> - KV cache warmup: Typical KV cache convergence depends on sequence distribution; for a warm-standby config we recommend a 15–40 minute warmup window to reach >90% hit rates for common prefixes.

Two questions: 1) Does Redwood provide a deterministic warm-up plan (e.g., replay the last N minutes of traffic or synthetic prefix sweep)? 2) If we choose to replay traffic from our end, do you recommend a particular rate limit so we don’t saturate the standby GPUs during the warmup?

Also: what happens to data residency during cross-region failover? We have EU PII customers and need to know whether the standby region will ever hold persistent copies of EU data or whether Redwood will gate data flows during failover.

Thanks — Ingrid

Ingrid Olsen

StratusPay

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 Jun 2028 11:00:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Draft addendum language and procurement notes (do not forward)

Sean / Neha — I drafted a tight addendum that addresses their asks. Key points included:

- Explicit ownership bullets: Redwood manages control-plane actions; customer responsible for DNS delegation unless managed-delegation is purchased.
- RTO/RPO table (Reserved/Warm/Cold) with exact minutes.
- A guardrail: If activation is initiated but deemed unsuccessful within 72 hours, we will roll back to original routing and issue a post-mortem.
- Temporary credit: 30% credit applied to compute charges for the first 72 hours of any unscheduled activation where the standby is used for customer traffic.
- Data residency: Add clause that Redwood will not persist long-term copies of EU-only PII in non-EU regions; caches and ephemeral KV state are allowed for operational purposes and will be deleted within X hours post-rollback.

I attached a working doc (sla-draft-standby-amendment.docx). Once you OK, I’ll send to Alex + Ingrid with track changes.

Kimberly Park
Director, Contracts & Legal
Redwood Inference

Alex / Ingrid — thanks for the great questions and for outlining procurement’s needs. Summary and clear next steps below so we can keep momentum: 

Summary:
- RTO/RPO: we will commit to the RTO/RPO table (Reserved: <=1m/0; Warm: 15–30m/<=5m; Cold: 1–4h/<=1h) in the addendum.
- Ownership: Redwood will drive control-plane actions and provide managed-delegation as an optional add-on. Customer remains responsible for signed access where required.
- KV warm-up: Redwood provides a warm-up API & recommended replay script. If StratusPay replays traffic we recommend starting at 25% of peak QPS for the first 10 minutes, then ramp to 50% for 10 minutes, then 100% as capacity stabilizes. We’ll include sample scripts in the drive link below.
- Data residency: Proposed clause (from Kimberly) that ephemeral caches may exist outside EU for the duration of an activation but persistent copies of EU-Personally Identifiable Information will not be retained in non-EU regions. Exact retention period and technical controls are in the draft.
- Billing: Redwood will offer a 30% pilot credit for the first 72 hours of any unscheduled activation during the pilot; permanent credit terms can be negotiated for production.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly to send the tracked addendum to StratusPay legal by Monday EOD.
2) If you approve the addendum language, we’ll propose a four-week pilot start window beginning as early as 2028-07-09 to validate recovery timelines.
3) I’ll share the pilot checklist and the warm-up scripts in the shared drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/standby-addendum/preview
